text:
maria: quick follow-up from yesterday's RFC review — we need a concrete plan for canary -> auto-fallback that handles both model-version and degradation (e.g. quantized, smaller model, or cached response).

maria: core constraints: preserve session semantics for chat (KV cache), minimize user-visible truncation, and avoid cascading fallbacks that thundering-herd on lower tiers.

devon: +1. also important: we must guarantee deterministic fallback ordering and expose that via the routing config so product teams can reason about costs.

oleg: what about making fallback operate at two levels: request-level (route to fallback model if latency/capacity fails) and token-level (stream switch to cached prefix or simplified LM)? Any runtime has opinions here.

liyah: token-level switches sound powerful but are stateful and will complicate KV cache validity. If we swap models mid-stream we need a cache compatibility matrix.

paul: can we decouple by adding a "compatibility tag" on model artifacts? e.g. model:v1+kv_compat:v1 -> router checks route policy before attempting token-level fallback.

maria: yes, compatibility tags + capability bits (supports_kv_cache, supports_stream_switch) — router should reject token-level fallback unless both source and target advertise support.

sre-bot: deploy: canary scheduled for 2026-04-05 03:00 UTC — watch for latency spike alerts.

devon: tradeoffs: if we require compat, fewer fallback options -> more request-level rollups. But safer. We should allow an escape hatch: forced degrade route that rewrites prompt to short-circuit KV usage (e.g., summarization) before falling back.

maria: suggestion: introduce 3-phase fallback policy per route: 
- primary variant list (ordered)
- degrade handlers (transform pipeline)
- circuit-breaker triggers (latency error %, token errors)
Router will evaluate in order.

oleg: show me a config example.

maria: code snippet:

```
route: chat_session_v1
primary: [model-44b-v2, model-44b-v1]
fallbacks:
  - type: model_variant
    candidates: [model-22b-quant, model-13b]
  - type: degrade_handler
    handler: short_summarize_then_generate
circuits:
  latency_p95_ms: 1200
  error_rate_pct: 2
```

liyah: small nit: we should separate rollout-weighted canaries from fallback ordering. Canary weights control live traffic distribution; fallbacks are only consulted when circuits trip or candidates fail.

paul: Agree. Operationally we need two primitives in the control plane: "traffic_labels" (for canary percentages) and "fallback_chains" (for automatic recovery).

devon: On metrics SLOs: fallback should attach a metric label like fallback_reason={timeout, oom, degraded_quality} and increment a per-route counter so we can alert if fallback rate accelerates.

maria: yes, and importantly we need an SLA for fallback quality: e.g., fallback_count/total_requests > 0.5 => auto pause canary and notify product. We must pick thresholds conservatively.

oleg: about KV cache: when falling back to smaller model we may not have compatible KV format. Proposal: router attempts a cheap validator call to target model with a 1-token probe that checks KV sync; if probe fails, router either runs degrade_handler or falls back to precomputed cached response.

liyah: probes add latency and extra qps. Maybe only enable probes for long sessions or when confidence is low. Short sessions can rely on request-level fallback.

paul: ops question: how do we avoid waterfalling fallback attempts? e.g., primary fails, router hits model-22b, which is saturated and times out -> router tries model-13b which also times out, producing N retries and extra load.

maria: solution: progressive backoff + single-flight per request id: the router should memoize an in-flight fallback decision for X ms, and broadcast the selected candidate to concurrent requests with the same route and session. Also cap attempts to N (default 2).

devon: single-flight is good. Also enforce backpressure: if candidate queue depth > threshold, skip to degrade_handler immediately.

oleg: long-term refactor idea: extract a "fallback policy service" that exposes an evaluation API: evaluate(route, session_state, metrics) -> next_action. This isolates complex logic from the router and makes it easier to A/B different strategies.

maria: yes, makes sense. Keep runtime fast-path cheap; call the policy service only on circuit triggers. Policy service can be async and pluggable.

liyah: testing: we'll need deterministic sim harness that replays production traces and forces various failures so we can validate behavior (no duplicate outputs, no KV corruption).

paul: also add a canary guard: if fallback_rate > X within 10 min window, automatically rollback canary weights to previous snapshot.

maria: next steps: i'll open a follow-up RFC with:
1) fallback policy primitives + config schema,
2) compat-tag registry and probe protocol,
3) runtime single-flight + cap semantics,
4) metrics/alerting contract,
5) test harness plan.

devon: ack. can I take the compat-tag registry section?

maria: please. oleg can take probe protocol. liyah owns metrics + alerts. paul will draft operational runbook. i'll wire RFC and link to this thread.

sre-bot: note: created issue #3214 for canary rollback automation.

maria: thanks all :raised_hands:

devon: :thumbsup:

oleg: :eyes:
